title: Exact constant finite free presentations after flat sheaf scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], $R$ a commutative ring, $R_{\mathcal C}$ its constant ring sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and $B$ a sheaf of commutative $R_{\mathcal C}$-algebras. For every $R$-module $P$, let $P_{\mathcal C}$ be the constant module sheaf [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and put $E_B(P)=B\otimes_{R_{\mathcal C}}P_{\mathcal C}$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then the functor $P\mapsto P_{\mathcal C}$ is exact and has the canonical finite-power identifications $(R^s)_{\mathcal C}\cong(R_{\mathcal C})^s$ for every finite $s\geq0$. The functor $E_B$ has natural identifications $\beta_s:E_B(R^s)\xrightarrow{\sim}B^s$ characterized locally by $b\otimes(x_i)\mapsto(bx_i)_i$, with inverse $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$. For every matrix $A:R^m\to R^n$ over $R$, these identify $E_B(A)$ with the matrix $A_B:B^m\to B^n$ whose entries are the images of those of $A$ in $B$. If $B$ is flat over $R_{\mathcal C}$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], every specified exact sequence $0\to R^m\xrightarrow{A}R^n\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$ with $m,n$ finite induces the exact sequence $0\to B^m\xrightarrow{A_B}B^n\xrightarrow{E_B(v)\beta_n^{-1}}E_B(P)\to0$. Independently of flatness, every specified isomorphism $R^r\xrightarrow{v}P$ with $r$ finite induces the isomorphism $B^r\xrightarrow{E_B(v)\beta_r^{-1}}E_B(P)$. All finite-power and matrix identifications include rank zero.

source.place: Tag 03EI, lemma-sheafification-exact; specialization to constant module presheaves and flat change of rings; blueprint main-20261015, det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc proof, Local models, exact pullback of the specified scalar presentation

proof.text: For an $R$-module $M$, write $cM$ for the constant module presheaf over the constant ring presheaf $cR$. Any exact sequence of $R$-modules gives an exact sequence of these presheaves: at every object its component is the original sequence, and presheaf kernels and cokernels are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact](1). By part (2) of the same node, sheafifying this sequence is exact. By [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor], its terms, maps and extended scalar actions are precisely $M_{\mathcal C}$ and the constant module maps in the statement. Exactness here also means exactness as $R_{\mathcal C}$-modules: kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafifications of sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so the extended actions do not change either construction. This proves exactness of the constant module functor.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), applied to the constant ring presheaf; Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian)

proof.text: For finite $s$, the coordinate projections give the equality $c(R^s)=(cR)^s$ of module presheaves. Sheafification preserves finite limits, hence finite products, by [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact](2). Sheafifying these projections therefore gives a canonical isomorphism $\alpha_s:(R^s)_{\mathcal C}\simeq(R_{\mathcal C})^s$, linear for the sheafified scalar action of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. It sends each constant basis vector to its coordinate basis section. The empty product in a module category is the zero module, so this also proves $\alpha_0:0_{\mathcal C}\simeq0$.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact): finite limits, applied to finite products of the constant module presheaf

proof.text: Use $\alpha_s$ to replace $(R^s)_{\mathcal C}$ by $(R_{\mathcal C})^s$. For every object $U$, put $D=R_{\mathcal C}(U)$ and $T=B(U)$. Define $T\otimes_DD^s\to T^s$ by $b\otimes(x_i)\mapsto(bx_i)_i$, and $T^s\to T\otimes_DD^s$ by $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes e_i$. The first map is balanced and $T$-linear; the second is $T$-linear. The composites are identities: one sends $(b_i)$ to $(b_i)$, and the other sends $b\otimes x$ to $\sum_i bx_i\otimes e_i=b\otimes\sum_i x_ie_i=b\otimes x$. These formulas commute with every restriction, so they are inverse isomorphisms of presheaves. The target $B^s$ is a sheaf, since compatible coordinate sections glue uniquely coordinate by coordinate. The sheafified tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] thus gives the required $B$-linear $\beta_s:E_B(R^s)\simeq B^s$ with the stated local formulas. They commute with scalar-algebra maps by the same formulas. For $s=0$ both sides are zero and the sum is empty. The tensor construction is functorial: on a module map $f$, it sends $b\otimes p$ to $b\otimes f_{\mathcal C}(p)$, and the identity and composition laws hold on these tensors and hence after sheafification. In Lean, the already proved scalar-extension lift, pure-tensor extensionality, restriction compatibility, and scalar-balancing API of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence] implement the same sheafified maps and the verification of their inverses. The constant basis decomposition is proved by sheafification-unit extensionality and finite coordinate expansion.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product): tensor as sheafification of sectionwise tensor; explicit finite free tensor formulas

proof.text: Write $A=(a_{ij})$ with $1\leq i\leq n$, $1\leq j\leq m$. Before sheafification, the $i$th coordinate of $A(x)$ is $\sum_j a_{ij}x_j$. Applying sheafification to this equality of maps, the coordinate identifications $\alpha_m,\alpha_n$ identify $A_{\mathcal C}$ with that same matrix over $R_{\mathcal C}$; these are the coordinate projections constructed in step 2 using [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor]. Write $\bar a_{ij}$ for its image in $B$. On a section $(b_j)$ of $B^m$, the composite $\beta_n E_B(A)\beta_m^{-1}$ is, using the tensor maps of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], $\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j\mapsto\sum_{i,j}b_j\otimes a_{ij}e_i\mapsto(\sum_j\bar a_{ij}b_j)_i$. This is exactly $A_B$, proving the matrix compatibility (and naturality for every map between finite free modules). If either rank is zero, the indicated sums are empty and the maps are the unique zero maps. The pure-tensor map formula from [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence] gives the stated sectionwise computation.

source.place: Section 03EK (section-tensor-product): functoriality and balancing; constant module sheafification as in Tag 03EI

proof.text: Apply step 1 to the specified sequence $0\to R^m\xrightarrow{A}R^n\xrightarrow{v}P\to0$. If $B$ is flat as an $R_{\mathcal C}$-module, [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] says that $-\otimes_{R_{\mathcal C}}B$ is an exact functor. Apply [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](a),(c): it preserves the initial monomorphism, the terminal epimorphism, and the zero middle homology. Interchanging the two tensor factors by $p\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes p$ identifies this with the sequence obtained by $E_B$; the interchange is a natural isomorphism because this balanced sectionwise map is its own inverse, and then sheafifies by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Exactness as $B$-modules follows from exactness on the underlying $R_{\mathcal C}$-modules: [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] computes kernels sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels for either scalar sheaf, giving the same underlying abelian sheaves. Conjugate the first two terms by $\beta_m,\beta_n$. Step 4 identifies the first arrow with $A_B$, and the second is precisely $E_B(v)\beta_n^{-1}$. This is the required short exact sequence, with the specified arrows.

source.place: Tag 03ER (definition-flat), item (3); Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian); exact-functor consequences as in Homology Tag 010N

proof.text: For a specified isomorphism $v:R^r\simeq P$, let $w$ be its inverse. Functoriality of constant sheafification [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and of tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives $E_B(w)E_B(v)=1$ and $E_B(v)E_B(w)=1$. Thus $E_B(v)\beta_r^{-1}$ has inverse $\beta_r E_B(w)$, without a flatness hypothesis. For $r=0$, both $P$ and $E_B(P)$ are zero, as the same formulas show. This completes all clauses.
